A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same URS research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original routing experiments, zero-shot generalization results, benchmark evaluations, and component ablations in Section 5 and Appendices I–K.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds scalability evaluations, controlled baseline comparisons, efficiency measurements, and further ablations.

M1.justification: v2 removes the proposed LLM-driven mask-generation, validation, and reuse pipeline described in v1 Section 4 and Appendix G. Constraint masking remains, but its automated generation is no longer part of the presented method. The UDR, MBM, hypernetwork, and reinforcement-learning backbone remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds AOP, APCTSP, and ASPCTSP evaluations, increasing reported coverage from 107 to 110 variants. It also adds synthetic CVRPTW, CVRPB, and OCVRPTW scenarios with 1,000–5,000 nodes and Set-AGS benchmarks with 3,000–7,000 nodes, substantially extending the tested input conditions.

E2.justification: RouteFinder already appeared in v1's Set-X comparison, but v2 newly evaluates RF-TE and CaDA on shared tasks and retrains both for a 48-variant comparison (Appendix J.2). ELG joins the benchmark comparisons. Conversely, the AM comparison on SPCTSP disappears between v1 Table 10 and v2 Table 15.

E3.justification: New protocols include 16 instances per synthetic large-scale setting, constraint-matched baseline evaluations, equal 150-epoch training for URS and retrained comparators, and disabling augmentation across UDR-component ablations. Appendix D also changes the stated ACVRP oracle from OR-Tools to PyVRP. These do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the original ablations, v2 tests training-problem selection, attention efficiency, separate BIAS/WEIGHT contributions on unseen tasks, removal of every UDR component, and hypernetwork versus adapter decoders (Appendices G, J.1, and K.5–K.7). These substantially expand evidence about component necessity, efficiency, and generalization.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and retain the same LKH3 one-run setting. No new training-seed information, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests are provided. v2 Figure 4 replots existing ablation values without error bars.

E6.justification: Numerous unseen-task values and rankings change: URS's OCVRPBPTW gap changes from -3.47% to 10.05%, falling behind the retained neural comparators (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 15). The cause is unspecified. v2 adds extensive scalability, baseline, and ablation results, while retaining the 11 seen-task and Set-X results. Some original comparator entries disappear.

T1.justification: v2 Table 13 adds explicit asymptotic time and space complexity comparisons absent from v1. The final probability formula also replaces v1 Equation 9's general mask with a visited-node condition in Equation 10, despite retaining broader feasibility masking in prose. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v2 drops automatic LLM-based constraint handling and its feasibility guarantee from the central contributions. It adds an explicit scalability claim up to 7,000 nodes and specifies 110 variants, including 99 unseen variants. The claim of being the first single neural solver covering over 100 variants remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations for ATSP degradation through symmetric-task bias, ReLD decoder weakness through hypernetwork optimization difficulty, and generalization through training-feature coverage. It interprets the new component and adapter experiments and adds dynamic VRPs as a future extension. The earlier LLM reliability and overfitting rationale is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds URS code-access information, the CPU specification, prize-generation details, and explicit documentation of URS-STL's 300-epoch schedule with decay at epoch 251. That schedule was unspecified in v1, so its disclosure does not establish a training change. Conversely, the LLM prompt, mask-generator code, and checker examples are removed.

R1.justification: v2 removes Appendix A.3's positioning against LLM algorithm-generation approaches, including EoH, ReEvo, HSEvo, and AHD-MCTS. It expands comparisons of attention efficiency and supported problem scales and adds references supporting the broader evaluations. ICAM and RouteFinder publication updates concern the same previously cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and methodology narrative are substantially rewritten and reorganized. The standalone LLM section disappears, parameter generation receives a dedicated discussion, and the experimental and ablation narratives expand substantially. Appendices G and J are repurposed, and new subsections extend Appendix K.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, separates the pipeline and MBM diagrams, removes the LLM diagram, expands Table 1, and splits the seen-task table. The original summary ablation table becomes Figure 4. Numerous new experimental tables substantially change the presentation, while existing appendix tables are reformatted.

improvement.justification: The matched and equally budgeted comparisons in Appendix J.2, component and adapter ablations in K.5–K.7, and scalability tests in Tables 5–6 address important gaps in v1's validation of generalization and design choices. Removing the LLM component reduces constraint-handling documentation, and unexplained score revisions remain a weakness. Nevertheless, the stronger experimental controls, diagnostic evidence, and reproducibility information provide a substantial net improvement.
